Introduction
What Makes Veterans Vulnerable to Addiction?

blocks.html: With all the research we have on addiction, we are unable to pinpoint the exact cause. We do, however, have a solid understanding of various factors that increase a person’s risk for developing a substance use disorder. When we look at Veterans, we know that the prevalence of trauma and PTSD can play a role in the development of an addiction.
blocks.text: With all the research we have on addiction, we are unable to pinpoint the exact cause. We do, however, have a solid understanding of various factors that increase a person’s risk for developing a substance use disorder. When we look at Veterans, we know that the prevalence of trauma and PTSD can play a role in the development of an addiction.

blocks.html: The VA reported that 7% of Veterans will have PTSD at some point in their life, which is higher than the 6% rate seen among the general population. Veterans who were deployed are 3 x more likely to develop PTSD than those who are not.

blocks.html: Veterans who experienced physical injury, and those who were prescribed controlled medications, may also be at a higher risk of developing a substance use disorder. Medications, such as pain medications, are highly addictive medications.

Addiction Among Veterans
How Common is Addiction Among Veterans?

blocks.html: The 2020 National Survey on Drug Use and Health: Veteran Adults allowed us to gain some insight into the prevalence of mental health concerns that Veterans have been living with. This showed that approximately 12% of veterans were living with a substance use disorder. Additional findings included that:
blocks.text: The 2020 National Survey on Drug Use and Health: Veteran Adults allowed us to gain some insight into the prevalence of mental health concerns that Veterans have been living with. This showed that approximately 12% of veterans were living with a substance use disorder. Additional findings included that:

items: 7 in every 10 Veterans were struggling with drinking
4 in every 10 Veterans were struggling with drugs
1 in every 8 Veterans were struggling with both alcohol and drug use

blocks.html: Another important detail to be mindful of is the presence of co-occurring mental health concerns. The same 2020 National Survey reported that 1 in every 3 Veterans was living with a serious mental illness and that approximately 1.1 million Veterans were living with a substance use disorder and a mental health concern.

Dallas Detox is a Texas Drug Rehab for Veterans

blocks.html: A common experience in addiction is a sense of loneliness and isolation. This happens because when we are in active addiction, our focus tends to be on our next use. This can pull us away from those close to us and create distance and discord. Some Veterans find that they struggle with these feelings before they develop a problem with substances. Some Veterans find that they have a hard time adjusting to civilian life after active duty and deployment. These feelings can be a contributing factor to the misuse of drugs and alcohol. Dallas Detox is a Veterans drug rehab located in Weatherford, Texas, that offers inpatient treatment options. This includes detoxification, inpatient rehab programming, aftercare planning, and support for alumni who find themselves struggling in their recovery. As a luxury detox center in Texas you will have semi-private accommodations and an ample amount of shared space to relax in. Our secluded ranch in Dallas gives you the opportunity to take a step back and breathe. Our treatment program is tailored to each individual that we work with, including dual-diagnosis treatment. Our staff will spend time determining which specialized treatment options you would benefit from, such as our groups for Veterans, men, women, young adults, college students, First Responders, and groups for members of the LGBTQ community. If you are a Veteran who has been struggling to reduce, control, or stop your use of substances, we want you to know that you do not have to walk this road alone. Our Texas drug rehab for Veterans can provide you with the support, compassion, and encouragement you need in the early stages of your recovery. We encourage you to call (817) 904-2197 to begin your journey with Dallas Detox today!
